result.title: From States to Dynamics: Detecting Rule Violations in OthelloGPT
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS workshop, Interpretability as a Science: Toward rigorous foundations for understanding LLMs; 20 pages, 16 figures total (including Appendix)
result.summary: Sequence models trained on game moves have been shown to encode world models, with structured linear probes revealing the underlying game states. World models, however, are inherently dynamic: in deterministic board games, a set of rules constrain how states evolve over time. We therefore ask if and how OthelloGPT, a transformer trained only on Othello move sequences, manifests the rules of the game in its activation space. We divide the rules of Othello, and symmetrically their violations, into three classes: placing a disc on an empty square (R1), flanking an opponent's disc (R2), and moving in turn (R3). We find that linear probes accurately separate legal from illegal moves, and also distinguish between the three kinds of rule violations. We introduce an unsupervised rule-violation detector based on the step length of activations between consecutive moves, which identifies illegal moves above chance. We further improve our detection metric by computing step length in the latent space of select sparse autoencoders. Together, we find that OthelloGPT follows game rules of Othello to a large extent, and that we can detect rule violations using structured detectors on model activations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察仅用棋谱训练的 OthelloGPT 是否在激活空间中体现 Othello 规则：用线性探针区分合法与非法落子并辨别三类违规，再以相邻步激活的「步长」及部分 SAE 潜空间构建无监督违规检测器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其从「状态」转向「动态」的激活诊断，以及用潜空间步长刻画状态转移是否合规，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要约束、以及推理步间状态更新如何度量。
